system.summary: Papal nunciature cipher: homophonic alphabet of 1- and 2-digit elements (e.g. A = 28|38|8), 1 as null/separator, dotted code groups; key reconstructed by Lasry 2020.
system.notes: Element boundaries are not marked; the split is ambiguous and was resolved with a language model.

prior_solution.where: Contemporary decifrati bound in Francia 3; J. Lestocquoy (ed.), Correspondance du nonce en France Prospero Santa Croce (1552-1554), Acta Nuntiaturae Gallicae 9 (1972); Lasry's key on DECODE R6-R10 (24 Oct 2020)

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Fetched R6-R10 pages, images, 2016 transcriptions, Lasry's key file and a 288-page PDF with the DECODE cookie.
Lasry's reconstructed key (DOC_R*_D320x) applied to the transcriptions with an it-cinquecento beam segmenter (decode.py); R8 matches its interlinear clear.
The attached PDF is Lestocquoy 1972 (Acta Nuntiaturae Gallicae 9); located all five letters by folio (nos. 67, 71, 112, 124, second letter of 23 Dec 1553), cipher passages printed deciphered.
Decrypts of R6, R7, R8, R10 agree with the printed text where the transcription is clean.
R9's three struck-through cipher lines, unprinted, read from the image through the cancellation strokes.
R9 fragments ('l'ar[mata]', 'aviso') fit the clear P.S. written below; the cancelled cipher is that P.S., abandoned.

Re-read R9's cancelled lines at full resolution; long stretches align under the key (Corsica, fortuna, come ne, dove, aviso del Strozzi): the cancelled cipher is the clear P.S. below, not printed in 1972.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): linked the 2016 DECODE transcriptions; saved decode.py output with Lasry's key for R6, R7, R8, R10; R9 cancelled lines from r9_cancelled.txt; Lestocquoy 1972 cited, not copied

Reading audit (George Lasry's test: can a reader build coherent sentences and translate them?). texts/R6, R7, R8, R10_decryption.md and r9_cancelled.txt read: Lasry's key on the volunteer transcription leaves holes or garble in almost every clause (docs/_check_reading.py: 5-9% of sentences clean); R9's cancelled lines give a few aligned words. All five entries relabelled decoded, not read; each note points to the reading, the decipherment printed in Lestocquoy 1972. Class already solved and method read from existing decipherment kept (the text is known from the print), but no reading is shown here until the printed text is transcribed or cited page by page; fraction_read unknown -> 0.

outcome.method_basis: All five cipher passages have contemporary decifrati bound in Francia 3 and are printed deciphered in Lestocquoy 1972 (Acta Nuntiaturae Gallicae 9); Lasry's key on DECODE R6-R10 (2020) was applied as a check, and with it the three unprinted cancelled lines of R9 were read as the clear postscript below them.
outcome.texts_withheld: The reading is the contemporary decifrati and Lestocquoy's printed decipherment (Acta Nuntiaturae Gallicae 9, 1972, in copyright), cited per entry and not copied here; the project's own decodes of the DECODE transcription are decoded, not read (reading audit, 22 Oct 2026).
outcome.notes: Read at the time and printed 1972; Lasry's key on DECODE since 2020. R9's cancelled cipher lines (unprinted) read here as the P.S. Catalogue entry 245 removed, no write-up.

texts.label: R6, no. 67, Poissy, 26 Mar 1553
texts.summary: Prospero Santa Croce, nuncio in France, to Cardinal Innocenzo del Monte. There is close dealing with the Duke, perhaps for money from merchants, a league or artillery on the excuse the Duke of Florence used at Siena.
texts.note: Lasry's key on the 2016 volunteer transcription: holes or garble in almost every clause (long [digit] runs, o/oa for d, {} leftovers). The reading is the contemporary decipherment printed in Lestocquoy 1972, pp. 157 ff., not copied (reading audit, 22 Oct 2026).

texts.label: R7, no. 71, Poissy, 5 Apr 1553
texts.summary: Prospero Santa Croce, nuncio in France, to Cardinal Innocenzo del Monte. The cipher passage printed by Lestocquoy pp. 162-163, on a supreme general for Italy with twenty thousand scudi.
texts.note: Lasry's key on the 2016 volunteer transcription: holes or garble in almost every clause (long [digit] runs, o/oa for d, {} leftovers). The reading is the contemporary decipherment printed in Lestocquoy 1972, pp. 162-163, not copied (reading audit, 22 Oct 2026).

texts.label: R8, no. 112, Abbaye d'Ourscamp, 28 Sept 1553
texts.summary: Prospero Santa Croce, nuncio in France, to Cardinal Innocenzo del Monte. The Most Christian King is displeased with the Corsica enterprise but resolves to maintain it, partly with provision of forty thousand scudi for the affairs of Parma.
texts.note: Lasry's key on the 2016 volunteer transcription: holes or garble in almost every clause (long [digit] runs, o/oa for d, {} leftovers). The reading is the contemporary decipherment printed in Lestocquoy 1972, p. 218, not copied (reading audit, 22 Oct 2026).

texts.label: R10, second letter of 23 Dec 1553
texts.summary: Prospero Santa Croce, nuncio in France, to Cardinal Innocenzo del Monte. Many urge His Majesty to make war in Italy.
texts.note: Lasry's key on the 2016 volunteer transcription: holes or garble in almost every clause (long [digit] runs, o/oa for d, {} leftovers). The reading is the contemporary decipherment printed in Lestocquoy 1972, pp. 243-244, not copied (reading audit, 22 Oct 2026).

texts.label: R9, no. 124, Paris, 14 Dec 1553: the three cancelled lines
texts.summary: Santa Croce to del Monte, 14 Dec 1553. Three struck-through cipher lines, not printed by Lestocquoy, which correspond to the clear postscript written below them: the royal fleet that left for Corsica has met a storm, no one knows where it is, and there is no news of Strozzi.
texts.note: Three cancelled lines read through the strokes, uncertain throughout: only a few stretches align with Lasry's key (port, Corsica, fortuna, Strozzi); the gist matches the clear postscript under them. The letter's text is in Lestocquoy 1972, p. 240 (reading audit, 22 Oct 2026).
